reason: The fast rocky projectiles appear to be the remaining stones the rocky world must pass through.

choice.combine: The rocky world with a small moon

expectation: The projectiles will strike the rocky world or its moon, advancing the first goal.

effect: The rocky world combined with its host star instead, completing the stones goal and widening the view to the system.
reaction: I was surprised the host star, rather than the projectiles, was the required partner.
reason: The exposed gas belongs at the exposed inner disk, which may show how disk material escapes.

choice.combine: Exposed gas carrying small dust grains

expectation: The exposed disk gas and dust will be released toward the surrounding galaxy.

effect: The exposed disk gas and dust escaped into the surrounding nursery, completing the remaining goal and clarifying that this happened early in the system's history.
reaction: The contrast between early disk escape and the rocky world's later collisions was interesting.

mostWorthwhile.text: Returning the exposed material to the surroundings connected the planetary disk back to the wider nursery and clarified the different timescales.

leastWorthwhile.text: The attempted collision with the projectiles was confusing: the world instead combined automatically with its host star.

surprise.text: I expected the projectiles to be the rocky world's partner, but the host star was required to complete that goal.

arbitrary.text: Using the host star rather than the visible projectiles felt somewhat arbitrary, although the result explained the widening view of the system.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: tracing how material moves between a planetary system and its surroundings was interesting, despite the confusing first combination.
